I've been working this same 6 mu for three decades. The wheat-maize rotation is what my father did and what everyone around here does. I know this land. My two kids work in Shijiazhuang now, so it's mainly me and my wife handling the farm. I need to keep it manageable.

**Wheat (planted October):**
I'll use the Jimai improved variety — reliable, the seed station nearby always has it, and I know how it behaves in my soil. I'll plough before planting to turn under the maize stalks properly, then apply compound fertilizer as base. I'll top-dress urea at jointing in March. I always irrigate four times: at sowing to ensure germination, a winter water in December if it's dry, jointing in April, and heading in May. Powdery mildew hits every few years so I'll spray once for that, plus herbicide in early spring and aphid spray before harvest — three pesticide runs total.

**Maize (planted June, right after wheat harvest):**
I use Zhengdan 958. Everyone in our village uses it and it performs well on our sandy loam. After wheat I just do rotary tillage — no need to plough deep again. Base fertilizer goes in at planting, then I side-dress nitrogen at the big bell stage. I irrigate at planting if it's dry, then definitely at tasseling and grain filling — three times. I spray once for corn borer and once for fall armyworm, which has been worse these last few years.

I won't change much from last year. When something works on your land for thirty years, you don't fix it without good reason.
